newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down, 5 cts in contango.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down, 5 cts in contango.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps weakened slightly late afternoon on Tuesday as a five-cent contango was established in the front months amid fears of a prompt oversupply in the physical market, traders said.
"The gas oil market is firmly in contango on fears of a prompt glut," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.75-$24.85 per barrel range, down about 10 cents from Monday, while July was quoted unchanged at $24.80-$24.90, brokers said.
June traded earlier in the day at $24.82 and July traded at $24.875 per barrel, they said.
Swaps traders said the weaker prices came despite large purchases by some traders who have since late last week bought more than two million barrels of June and July paper.
The same traders have also lent considerable support to the physical market, buying over 20 million barrels of gas oil since March 3.
But over the past few weeks, these traders have slowed down their purchases compared to the record 2.44 million barrels they bought in one-day in late April.

The supply overhang was clearly seen on Monday when eight sellers emerged to sell at least ten 150,000-barrel cargoes at around the $25.00 per barrel free-on-board Singapore mark with one cargo traded at $24.80 per barrel.
The deal was struck for the lowest offer with other sellers holding out at just over this price against bids at $24.70-24.80 per barrel.
In addition to the poor demand in Singapore, prices are also under pressure due to reduced Chinese demand as traders drop their prices to capture bigger market share.
Industry sources said that the traders who have bought record volumes in the Singapore physical market are now desperately trying to offload their cargoes in China.
As a result Chinese prices have fallen to just over $190.00 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis from about $200.00 about one month ago.
Traders said firmer July prices are partly due to market hope that Chinese demand will pick up then.
June fuel oil was last quoted down about 25 cents from Monday at $100.25/$101.00 per tonne, brokers said.
